bull.t: Recurring Starlink revenue and subscriber growth
bull.b: Large, growing recurring consumer and enterprise Starlink revenue provides durable, predictable cash flows and scale economies. Stable ARPU and rising enterprise/government mix diversify monetization, improve adjusted EBITDA resilience, and support long-term network ROI as constellation capacity grows.

A very large cash position and sizable backlog materially reduce near-term funding risk and enable multi-year CapEx plans. This financial cushion supports aggressive constellation, compute and launch scale without immediate refinancing, lowering execution funding sensitivity over the medium term.

bull.t: Rapid AI/compute traction and contracted cloud wins
bull.b: Fast-growing compute revenue and large contracted cloud agreements diversify revenue beyond launches and connectivity. Short payback on new compute deployments and improving AI adjusted EBITDA suggest a scalable, high-margin service line that leverages existing infrastructure and supports durable revenue expansion.

bear.t: Heavy capital expenditures and negative free cash flow
bear.b: Sustained, very high CapEx drives persistent negative free cash flow, increasing reliance on capital markets despite large cash balances. If elevated investment intensity continues, long-term returns depend on timely monetization of assets; funding needs and dilution risk remain structural vulnerabilities.

A swing to material consolidated losses despite gross margin gains signals that rapid scale is outpacing near-term operating leverage. Persistent segment-level losses can erode returns on invested capital and mean that top-line growth alone may not translate into sustainable net profitability without structural spending moderation or monetization gains.

bear.t: Execution and regulatory timing risk for flagship programs
bear.b: Revenue and margin upside from Starship and V3 satellites depend on successful flights, recoveries, certifications and spectrum/launch timelines. Delays or regulatory setbacks would postpone monetization, extend high CapEx periods, and amplify funding and execution risk across connectivity and launch businesses.
